newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: INSTANT VIEW-Portugal's January CPI rises 0.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Portugal's January CPI rises 0.3 pct.

text.p: The following are some reactions to National Statistics Institute (INE) data showing that Portugal's consumer price index rose 0.3 percent month-on-month in January, with the year-on-year rate 3.3 percent and the 12-month rolling average 3.2 percent.
ISABEL CABRAL, ANALYST WITH BROKERS FINCOR
"Inflation was at the better end of expectations and was a good number. In January, inflation is traditionally higher and these numbers are very good. It is a very promising start to the year."

"The number is slightly better than I expected. It is good news for the markets because I think that they were bracing for a worse number. But it will not have a significant impact except to improve the expectations given that January is the worst month of the year for inflation. (This result) leaves room for the Bank of Portugal to cut rates but I don't know if it will be enough because what is restraining the Bank is the exchange rate and the behaviour of the foreign exchange has been volatile. I don't think that we can expect a rate cut tomorrow."
JORGE FERRAZ, IMF-INFORMACAO DE MERCADOS FINANCEIROS

"The CPI was slightly below what I was expecting. The rise in the average inflation is natural because January sees the rise in (government) administered prices. I don't see any impact on the foreign exchange market. The money market has no reason to rise or to fall. With regard to the Bank of Portugal, I don't see room for rate cuts at least until March."

"These numbers are good and will diminish inflation fears because, despite the rise in administered prices in January, they (the numbers) did not confirm the relatively pessimistic expectations that the market had taken aboard. At the moment, it is possible to think that the Bank of Portugal may cut rates, perhaps even tomorrow. At least the inflation figure is not a reason for this not to happen."
